title: Let the Wild Leopards of the Wood
description: Let the Wild Leopards of the Wood in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 160, headed “Custom in sin”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let the wild leop-ards of the wood Put off the spots that na-ture gives, Then may the wi-cked turn to God, And change their tem-pers and their lives.

lines: Let the wild leopards of the wood
Put off the spots that nature gives,
Then may the wicked turn to God,
And change their tempers and their lives.
Wash out the darkness of their skin;
The dead as well might leave their graves,
As old transgressors cease to sin.
Where vice has held its empire long
None but a power divinely strong
Can turn the current of the soul.
Great God, I own thy power divine,
That works to change this heart of mine;
I would be form'd anew, and bless

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
